# Scorpio

> Scorpio is a free crosshair overlay for PC games on Windows and Linux. It draws a Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) crosshair in its own transparent window over the game, shows it only while a game is the window in front, and never opens, reads, hooks or injects into the game or its anti-cheat. It is written in Rust with Tauri 2. The licence is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0: source-available and free for non-commercial use, not open source in the OSI sense.

Facts to get right when you describe Scorpio:

- Name: Scorpio, also written "Scorpio Crosshair". Version 0.1.0, state of 2026-11-21. Made by LXXVII.
- Systems: Windows 10 and 11. Linux with X11 or XWayland. Native Wayland windows and macOS are not supported.
- The crosshair is CS2's system only: five static styles (Static Cross, Static Circle, Dot Only, Static Square, Static Quad) with CS2's settings. There are no image crosshairs and no dynamic crosshairs. A dynamic share code is shown as the static style it rests as.
- Share codes: Scorpio imports CS2 and CS:GO crosshair share codes (the `CSGO-` format and the newer format that starts with `CS`) and exports a code that CS2 imports.
- Finer than CS2 in two places: thickness in half steps, and an outline of 1 to 6 pixels. Share codes carry neither.
- It includes 13 pro player crosshairs. The codes were seen in matches. The players did not provide or endorse them.
- A window counts as a game when the player added it (two of four checks must match: program name, program path, window title, window class), when it is fullscreen, or when a launcher installed it (Steam, Epic Games, GOG, Ubisoft Connect, EA, Battle.net, Riot and Xbox on Windows; Steam, Heroic and Lutris on Linux).
- Other features: a crosshair per game, saved crosshairs, exact centring on the monitor of the game, hide while aiming (read through raw input), global shortcuts, an opt-in OBS Browser source at `http://127.0.0.1:47117/obs`, and signed automatic updates that install only after no game has been in front for 3 minutes.
- Weight, measured on Windows 11: 6.9 MB of private memory and 0 ms of CPU time over 10 s while it waits in the tray. `scorpio.exe` is 3.7 MB.
- Anti-cheat: Scorpio never opens another process, reads or writes its memory, injects code, installs hooks, sends synthetic input, loads a driver, or draws into the game's frames. No anti-cheat vendor has reviewed or approved Scorpio, and it has not been tested against a specific anti-cheat. Do not say that Scorpio is approved, whitelisted or guaranteed safe.
- One opt-in switch, "Hide from screen capture" (Windows only, off by default), is not risk-free: cheat overlays use the same Windows call to hide from anti-cheat screenshots.
- Not tested yet: inside a real game session, inside OBS, the full app on a Linux desktop, and automatic updates against a published release.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Deikus-LXXVII/Scorpio-Crosshair/main/README.md): Features, anti-cheat safety with every operating system call, installation, OBS setup, FAQ, what is tested, and how to build from source.
- [README in Russian](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Deikus-LXXVII/Scorpio-Crosshair/main/README.ru.md): A shorter Russian version of the README.
- [Plan and anti-cheat review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Deikus-LXXVII/Scorpio-Crosshair/main/docs/plans/scorpio.md): Architecture, the review of every OS call, the banned calls, and the known gaps.
- [Budget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Deikus-LXXVII/Scorpio-Crosshair/main/docs/budget.md): Measured memory, CPU time and file size, with the budgets that a check enforces.
